questions.question: What is the Earth's axis, and how long does one spin take?
questions.expected_answer: The axis is an imaginary line through the middle of the Earth from the North Pole to the South Pole. The Earth spins around its axis from west to east. One complete spin takes about 24 hours, which is one day.

questions.question: Explain why we have day and night.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun can light only the half of the Earth that faces it, so that half has day, and the half facing away has night. As the Earth spins, each place turns into the sunlight, giving sunrise and day, and then turns away again, giving sunset and night. The Sun does not switch off; it is always shining.

questions.question: Why does the Sun seem to move across the sky, and how do shadows change during the day?
questions.expected_answer: The Earth spins from west to east, so the Sun only seems to rise in the east, move across the sky and set in the west. Shadows form on the side of an object away from the Sun. They are long in the morning and late afternoon and shortest around midday, and they point in a different direction as the day goes on.
